summary: Frontend-only verification of two scoped changes in /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx: (1) Crop tool drag smoothness — all 4 corner handles (tl/tr/bl/br) and the body drag moved cleanly and STAYED at their new positions with no snap-back across multiple sample drags (fresh state per corner, inward directions to avoid clamp). Zero console errors during drags. Confirm button applied the current (post-drag) rect and closed the modal — re-opening crop showed new imageDims (aspect ratio changed from 2:3 to ~4:5), verifying non-stale rect used. Cancel closes without changes. (2) Header toolbar order verified left→right: editor-close-button (x=14) → editor-header-save-button (x=66) → editor-title-button (x=131) → editor-zoom-reset (x=280) → editor-undo-button (x=332). Gap between Close and Save = 8px (>= 2px). Only 1 save button in DOM. Title button opens showTitleModal. Close navigates back to /.
critical_code_review_comments: CropModal PanResponders are now correctly created once via useRef; closures read cropRect/displayed from refs, so handler identity is stable across renders — this is the correct fix for the snap-back RCA.
editor.tsx is ~1750 lines; consider splitting CropModal, renderElement, and toolbar into separate modules for maintainability (non-blocking).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Both scoped changes verified via Playwright on the Expo web preview. Corner-drag test must open crop fresh per handle and drag INWARD (dx,dy pointing toward rect interior) to avoid clamping masking the assertion. Initial run with outward drags on already-maxed rect will show moved_and_stayed=false due to clamping, not snap-back.
rca_of_issue: Task 1 RCA (already fixed): Previously PanResponder.create was called on every render inside the component body. React re-attached new panHandlers on the underlying View mid-gesture; RN's touch system then referenced stale closures and effectively restarted the gesture with stale start coords, so on mouse-up the rect appeared to snap back to a previous position. The fix wraps each PanResponder in useRef(...).current (created once) and reads cropRect/displayed via refs kept fresh by useEffect, so handler identity is stable while still respecting latest state.
